question.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of the Roman Republic.
question.text: The government of the early Roman Republic was dominated by these upper-class citizens, who are often contrasted with the working-class plebeians [pleh-BEE-unz].
question.clue: They were identified by shoes of red leather, an iron ring, and a broad purple stripe worn down the right side of their tunics.

swap.leadin: This emperor killed his mother Agrippina the Younger and his first wife Octavia and forced Seneca the Younger to commit suicide for his alleged involvement in the Pisonian Conspiracy.
swap.text: Name this Roman emperor who was the first emperor to commit suicide, after learning that he had been sentenced to death in absentia.
swap.answerHtml: Nero [accept Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, but do NOT accept Claudius, Caesar, Augustus, or Germanicus alone]
swap.clue: This emperor remarked that he had "begun to live like a human being" after his Domus Aurea was finished.

question.leadin: Answer the following about some of Rome's best emperors.
question.text: This second of the group known as "the Five Good Emperors" expanded the Empire to its largest extent and is famous for his namesake column.
question.clue: This man sacked Ctesiphon, capital of the Parthian Empire, and commemorated his victory against the Dacians ] in a namesake "Column."

swap.leadin: Name some buildings constructed by the Romans.
swap.text: This stadium, which predated the Republic of Rome, had a large track that was used for chariot racing, but today only a patch of grassland remains.
swap.clue: Tacitus claimed the Great Fire started near this location, where a series of dolphins were flipped to count the number of times that quadrigas successfully made it past two turning points called metae.

question.leadin: One man of this name was a founder of the Roman Republic.
question.text: Give this name shared by Lucius Junius and the more famous Marcus Junius, who led the conspirators in assassinating Julius Caesar.
question.clue: A man with this name partnered with the husband of Lucretia to overthrow Tarquin the Proud, the last king of Rome.

swap.leadin: Congratulations, you are a merchant traveling from Mediolanum to the Eternal City of Rome in 71 BC! Answer the following about what you experience.
swap.text: Travel is quite easy to Rome as you travel on some of the 250,000 miles of these structures. A medieval proverb claims all of these structures "lead to Rome."
swap.clue: One of these structures was called "Salaria" for its role in the salt trade.

question.leadin: The Praetorian Guard had a habit of murdering Roman emperors.
question.text: This emperor was murdered by the Praetorian Guard in 41 C་E. The Praetorian Guard found this man's successor Claudius hiding behind a curtain.
question.answerHtml: Caligula [or Gaius Caesar Augustus Germanicus; reject any single part of his full name]
question.clue: While accompanying his father Germanicus on campaign as a child, this emperor received the nickname "little boots."

swap.text: This emperor's wife Agrippina the Younger supposedly killed him with poisonous mushrooms so her son could take the throne. This emperor ascended the throne after Caligula's assassination and launched an invasion of Britain.
swap.clue: His first wife was Urgulanilla, while his third was the supposedly promiscuous Messalina.

question.leadin: Identify these other kings of Rome.
question.text: This second king of Rome is credited with establishing the religious traditions of the city including the Vestal Virgins and the cults of Mars and Jupiter.
question.clue: This king, the second to rule Rome. This Sabine king built the Temple of Janus and made January the first month, in addition to setting the calendar at 365 days.

swap.leadin: He built the Cloaca Maxima and acquired the Sibylline books, but his son's crime and his overbearing demeanor led to his overthrow by Lucius Brutus.
swap.text: Name this last king of Rome, whose character was reflected in his cognomen.
swap.clue: This ruler took refuge with Aristodemus of Cumae after a battle in which Castor and Pollux purportedly fought against him.

question.text: This woman and leader of the Iceni rebelled in England against the governor Suetonius Paulinus during the reign of Nero. She was defeated at Watling Street, and may have poisoned herself after the battle.
question.clue: This person's popularity as a patriotic symbol in Victorian Britain was influenced by the theory that her name comes from a root meaning "victory" in Celtic.

swap.text: Ancient inhabitants of modern day Tuscany, among their famous representatives are Lars Porsenna who attempted to reinstall Tarquin the Proud. They were the dominant civilization in Italy until the rise of the Romans
swap.clue: The mutually recognized need to maintain defenses against these people led to the agreement to hold the combat of the Curiatti and Horatii proposed by Tullus Hostilius and accepted by the Albans.

question.text: As part of his reunification of the Roman Empire, Aurelian was forced to abandon this Roman province north of the Danube, which had been established by Trajan after conquering a namesake tribe under King Decebalus.
question.answerHtml: Dacia [or Roman Dacia or Dacia Traiana or Dacia Felix; accept Dacians]
question.clue: Soldiers of this region used the sickle-like falx during a war in which a bridge near the Iron Gates was built by Apollodorus.

swap.text: This member of the First Triumvirate led the campaign that defeated Mithridates for good. He was assassinated in Egypt after Julius Caesar completely routed his forces at Pharsalus.
swap.clue: Aulus Gabilius granted this man special power to fight a certain menace across the entire Mediterranean; his son Sextus later emulated that menace by becoming a pirate.

question.leadin: Answer the following about attacks on Roman control in Hispania.
question.text: This former shepherd and leader of the Lusitani rose up against Roman control after a governor dug a trench around a group of Lusitani and killed them while they were surrendering their weapons. This leader defeated a Roman army at the Battle of Mt. Veneris.
question.clue: Polybius called the long struggle with this leader of the Lusitanians the "War of Fire" for its violence. Wildly successful against Rome on the battlefield, he was killed in his sleep by three bribed Tartessian assassins.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about an object called the vitta ("WIT-tuh"), which was made of wool and worn over the hair together with the infula.
swap.text: These people often wore a white vitta and infula together with the suffibulum. These people, who guarded the Palladium, could be buried alive as a punishment for incestum ("een-KEST-um").
swap.clue: According to Plutarch, these people were punished by being sealed in a chamber near the Colline Gate with only limited food and water.

question.text: Prior to his dictatorship, Cincinnatus was most known in Roman politics for the large fine he had to pay after his son fled a death sentence for physically interfering with holders of this office.
question.answerHtml: tribune of the people [or plebeian tribune; or tribuni plebis]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about dubious accounts of sexual excess in European history.
swap.text: Livy states that the rites dedicated to this Roman god of wine and revelry were so debaucherous, murderous, and vice-ridden that the Senate suppressed them in 186 BC.
swap.answerHtml: Bacchus [accept Bacchanalia; do not accept or prompt on Dionysus]

question.leadin: Answer the following about the phrase "In hoc signo vinces," FTPE.
question.text: The story of vision of the cross was told by this lackey of Constantine, a historian from Caesarea who described the early years of Christianity in his Ecclesiastical History.
question.clue: The man who baptized Constantine had this name. A more famous Roman with this name was a Bishop of Caesarea who wrote an Ecclesiastical History of the early church.

swap.leadin: This commander fought a hopeless war against Vespasian and surrendered to the Romans after his troops committed suicide by killing every third man after the Siege of Yodfat.
swap.text: Identify this enemy of the Romans who, after the aforedescribed incident, became a citizen of the Roman Empire. He is best known for his histories on the "Antiquities" and the "War" of his home people.
swap.clue: Beginning with the Maccabean revolt and ending at Masada, this writer recounts the rise and downfall of his people in De Bello Judaico.
